P3400.d: P3400 is the bank-level verdict: the engine computer has concluded that cylinder deactivation on bank 1 as a whole does not behave as commanded, without blaming a single circuit. Makers fill it differently.
s: Rough idle or misfire codes on the deactivating cylinders
Ticking or clattering from the valve train
Reduced-cylinder mode no longer used, higher fuel use
c: Deactivation oil control valve or its screen clogged by debris
Low oil level, wrong grade or overdue oil change
Switchable rocker arm or lifter broken, dislodged or not latching
Oil pressure too high on cold start, e.g. weak relief valve spring
Engine control software needing an update

P3401.d: P3401 points to a broken control path to the solenoid that switches off cylinder 1, a cylinder that GM and Chrysler V8s and Ford's 1.5 l three-cylinder EcoBoost all deactivate. On the 2019 L84 and L86 V8s, GM looks at the low-side output while it is off: over 200 kilohm to ground counts as open, and 20 failures among 25 readings at 250 ms intervals make it a Type B fault.
s: Check engine lamp on, on GM after the second trip
c: Control wire broken or worn through, e.g. by a hot exhaust heat shield
Loose, corroded or oil-soaked solenoid connector
Open coil in the cylinder 1 deactivation solenoid
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

P3402.d: This code reports that cylinder 1 does not respond as expected when the engine computer switches it off or back on, although the control circuit itself tests fine. Ford lists P3402 in its Variable Displacement Engine monitor for 2020-2023 gasoline engines: it runs continuously during deactivation, entry and exit, between 400 and 4500 rpm and once oil pressure has had about two seconds to build.
s: Shudder or jerk when the engine enters or leaves reduced-cylinder mode
Cylinder deactivation no longer used, higher fuel use
c: Low oil level, wrong viscosity or aged oil slows the hydraulic switching
Switchable lifter or rocker of cylinder 1 sticking or not latching
Deactivation solenoid valve sticking or its oil screen blocked
Leaking solenoid seal lets control pressure bleed off

P3403.d: The engine computer drives the deactivation valve for cylinder 1 through an output stage that checks its own wiring. P3403 means that check found the control line pulled to ground.
s: Check engine lamp on after two trips
Engine no longer switches to reduced-cylinder mode
c: Control wire chafed against the engine and shorted to ground
Internal short in the cylinder 1 deactivation solenoid
Oil or water in the solenoid connector
Faulty output driver in the engine control module

P3404.d: P3404 is the short-to-power counterpart within the cylinder 1 group. GM tests it while the low-side driver is switched on: if the output still shows less than 0.5 ohm to supply voltage, the current has no proper path through the solenoid, and 20 of 25 samples at 250 ms set a Type B fault.
s: Possible further circuit codes on other solenoids if a shared supply is affected
c: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage in the harness
Shorted winding in the cylinder 1 deactivation solenoid
Damaged output stage in the engine control module

P3405.d: J2012 reserves P3405 for an open control circuit of a separate exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 1. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Cylinder deactivation or valve switching disabled
c: Broken wire or loose terminal to the exhaust valve actuator
Open coil in the cylinder 1 exhaust valve actuator
Output driver fault in the engine control module

P3406.d: Where an engine controls the exhaust valves of cylinder 1 separately, P3406 would mean the exhaust side does not follow the command although the circuit checks pass. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Rough running or vibration in reduced-cylinder mode
c: Insufficient or degraded oil delays exhaust-side switching
Exhaust lifter or rocker of cylinder 1 not latching or unlatching

P3407.d: P3407 stands for a short to ground in the control circuit of a dedicated exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 1. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, so there are no published thresholds.
c: Actuator control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the exhaust valve actuator
Engine control module output stage fault

P3408.d: If an engine has its own actuator for the exhaust valves of cylinder 1, P3408 marks a control circuit that reads high, usually a short to battery voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Shorted coil in the exhaust valve actuator
Output stage fault in the engine control module

P3409.d: P3409 is the open-circuit code for the deactivation control of cylinder 2. GM uses it on two very different engines.
s: Oil residue around the valve cover control valve (V6)
No reduced-cylinder operation, higher fuel use
c: Oil leaking at the control valve and soaking its connector (GM 3.6 L V6)
Broken wire or loose pin in the cylinder 2 solenoid circuit
Open coil in the cylinder 2 deactivation solenoid
Engine control module output driver fault

P340A.d: P340A is meant for engines that switch the intake valves of a whole bank through a shared control circuit, rather than one solenoid per cylinder. It reports an electrical fault in that bank 1 circuit, without saying whether it is open or shorted.
s: Higher fuel consumption at light load
c: Damaged, open or shorted wire in the bank 1 control circuit
Corroded or loose connector at the bank 1 actuator
Bank 1 intake deactivation actuator with open or shorted coil
Output stage fault in the engine control module

P340B.d: P340B mirrors P340A for bank 2, the bank that does not contain cylinder 1, so it only applies to V or boxer engines. It marks an electrical fault in a control circuit that switches the intake valves of that whole bank at once.
s: Engine runs on all cylinders permanently
c: Chafed, open or shorted wire to the bank 2 actuator
Oil or moisture in the bank 2 actuator connector
Defective bank 2 intake deactivation actuator coil
Engine control module output stage fault

P340C.d: P340C concerns a separate electrical circuit that disables the exhaust valves of bank 1 as a group. A fault in its wiring, connector or actuator coil sets the code.
c: Open or shorted wire in the bank 1 exhaust actuator circuit
Exhaust deactivation actuator coil open or shorted
Connector or wiring damaged by heat near the exhaust side
Engine control module output stage fault

P340D.d: P340D is the bank 2 version of the exhaust-side group circuit: the engine computer sees an electrical fault on the line that is supposed to disable the exhaust valves of the bank without cylinder 1. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Engine no longer drops cylinders at light load
c: Damaged wiring to the bank 2 exhaust deactivation actuator
Faulty coil in the bank 2 exhaust actuator
Output stage fault in the engine control module

P3410.d: P3410 covers a cylinder 2 deactivation system that is electrically intact but does not do what is commanded, such as valves that keep opening or fail to return. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Misfire on cylinder 2, often after a reduced-cylinder phase
c: Oil bleeding past the control valve seal, pressure lost
Rocker or lifter of cylinder 2 not latching
Broken solenoid tip left in the bore keeps a new valve from seating

P3411.d: P3411 means the control output for the cylinder 2 deactivation valve sees a short to ground. GM lists it for the L84 V8 (2019), whose Dynamic Fuel Management can switch off any cylinder: below 0.5 ohm to ground with the low-side driver off, 20 failures in 25 samples every 250 ms, at least 11 V on the powertrain relay and 425 rpm.
s: Check engine lamp after two trips
Dynamic Fuel Management inactive, engine stays on all cylinders
c: Damaged insulation lets the control wire touch ground

P3412.d: On GM's L84 V8 each cylinder, including cylinder 2, has a valve lifter oil solenoid bolted into the block valley. NHTSA's description of the system notes these solenoids are driven with peak-and-hold current for fast response.
c: Control wire shorted to a voltage feed in the harness
Low-resistance coil in the cylinder 2 solenoid
Engine control module output stage fault

P3413.d: P3413 belongs to the exhaust half of the cylinder 2 block and reports an open control circuit for a separately driven exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Open wire or connector to the cylinder 2 exhaust actuator

P3414.d: P3414 would be set when the exhaust valves of cylinder 2 do not follow a deactivation or reactivation command on an engine with separate exhaust valve control. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Rough running when cylinders are switched off
Deactivation suspended by the engine computer
c: Exhaust-side lifter or rocker of cylinder 2 not switching
Low oil pressure or aerated oil

P3415.d: P3415 describes a control circuit for a dedicated cylinder 2 exhaust valve actuator that is pulled toward ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 2 exhaust actuator touching ground
Internal short in the cylinder 2 exhaust actuator
Damaged output stage in the engine control module

P3416.d: P3416 means the control line of a separate cylinder 2 exhaust valve actuator sits too high, typically because it touches a supply voltage or the coil has shorted turns. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Actuator control wire shorted to a supply line
Shorted turns in the cylinder 2 exhaust actuator coil
Engine control module output stage fault

P3417.d: P3417 flags a broken path in the drive circuit of the cylinder 3 deactivation solenoid. GM documents it twice: its 2007 Displacement on Demand table covers solenoid circuits on cylinder 1, 3 and 5 and needs 30 bad readings in 100 with the engine turning faster than 800 rpm; for the 2019 DFM engine L84, the ECM expects over 200 kohm whenever its low-side output rests, 20 of 25 checks, Type B.
c: Broken or chafed wire between control module and cylinder 3 solenoid
Open winding in the cylinder 3 deactivation solenoid
Loose, oily or corroded solenoid connector
Failed output stage in the engine control module

P3418.d: P3418 is meant for a cylinder 3 deactivation that is wired correctly yet does not respond as requested: the cylinder keeps breathing when it should rest, or fails to come back. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Shudder when the engine changes between modes
c: Low oil level, wrong viscosity or aged oil
Lifter or rocker of cylinder 3 not locking or unlocking
Cylinder 3 control valve sticking or its screen blocked
Oil pressure too high or too low for the switching window

P3419.d: P3419 says the line feeding the cylinder 3 deactivation solenoid is dragged toward ground. The L84 V8 in GM's 2019 OBD documents shows the test: while the low-side output rests, a resistance to chassis ground under half an ohm is wrong, and once 20 out of 25 readings, one every 250 ms, agree, with the powertrain relay above 11 V and the engine at 425 rpm or faster, a Type B fault is logged.
s: Check engine lamp after two drives
Engine no longer drops cylinders under light load
c: Insulation of the cylinder 3 control wire worn through to ground
Internal short of the cylinder 3 solenoid to its housing
Oil or water bridging pins in the connector
Defective driver in the engine control module

P341A.d: P341A is the function check behind P340A: the bank 1 intake deactivation circuit is electrically sound, yet the valves do not end up where they were commanded. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Jerk or vibration when cylinders switch off or on
c: Low oil level or aged, contaminated oil
Bank 1 deactivation control valve sticking or screen blocked
Switchable lifters or rockers on bank 1 not latching or releasing
Insufficient oil pressure from a worn pump or leaking seal

P341B.d: With P341B the controller judges that intake deactivation on bank 2 is not doing its job even though no circuit fault is present: cylinders keep breathing when they should be sealed, or stay sealed after reactivation. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Rough running, mostly at light load
c: Oil level too low or oil past its service life
Lifter or rocker on bank 2 stuck in one switching state
Control valve on bank 2 sticking or leaking past its seal

P341C.d: P341C covers exhaust valves on bank 1 that ignore a deactivation command while their wiring and actuator coil check out. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Popping or uneven exhaust note in reduced-cylinder mode
c: Exhaust-side lifter or rocker on bank 1 not switching
Low oil pressure or foaming oil

P341D.d: P341D appears once the bank 2 exhaust valves respond wrongly to a deactivation or reactivation request while the electrical side is intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Bump or shudder during mode changes
c: Exhaust lifter or rocker on bank 2 switching late or not at all
Oil too thin, too old or too low for fast switching

P3420.d: P3420 reports that the cylinder 3 deactivation control line carries supply voltage where the module expects to pull it low. On GM's L84 the test runs only while the low-side output is switched on: a connection to battery voltage below 0.5 ohm, confirmed in 20 out of 25 samples, sets a Type B code.
c: Control wire of cylinder 3 touching a powered conductor
Shorted turns in the cylinder 3 solenoid winding
Output transistor in the engine control module damaged

P3421.d: P3421 opens the exhaust group of cylinder 3 and stands for an interrupted circuit to an actuator that would switch only the exhaust valves. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Broken lead or loose terminal at the cylinder 3 exhaust actuator
Fault in the control module output

P3422.d: P3422 would apply if cylinder 3's exhaust valves disregard an order to stop or restart even though the wiring checks out. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Fuel trim or misfire codes alongside
c: Exhaust-side switching lifter or rocker of cylinder 3 stuck
Oil level or quality outside specification
Restricted oil passage to the exhaust switching element

P3423.d: P3423 points to a grounded control wire at a dedicated cylinder 3 exhaust actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and NHTSA's 2025 look at GM's DFM engines shows why: each cylinder has just one lifter oil solenoid, and it feeds both lifters, intake and exhaust, so there is no separate exhaust output that could fail.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 3 shorted to engine ground
Actuator winding shorted to its housing
Faulty output stage in the control module

P3424.d: P3424 closes the cylinder 3 block and stands for an exhaust actuator control line that is held at supply voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Engine runs on all cylinders permanently
c: Exhaust actuator wire chafed against a supply line
Shorted turns in the exhaust actuator of cylinder 3

P3425.d: Cylinder 4 is one of the four cylinders that classic V8 cylinder deactivation shuts off, together with 1, 6 and 7, both at GM (Active Fuel Management) and on the Chrysler 5.7 L Hemi with MDS. That makes P3425 one of the best documented codes in this range.
s: Further circuit codes for cylinders 1, 6 and 7 if the shared harness is damaged
c: Solenoid harness chafed through by the exhaust manifold heat shield (5.7 L Hemi)
Open coil in the cylinder 4 deactivation solenoid
Control module software needing an update (Chrysler TSB 18-002-25)

P3426.d: P3426 is one of the few performance codes in this range that makers really use. FCA calls it Cylinder 4 Deactivation Control Performance on the 6.4 l Heavy Duty Hemi with MDS; bulletins 18-082-16 and 18-036-20 list it with P3402, P3442 and P3450 and fix it with new PCM software.
s: Misfire on cylinder 4 or rough running
Drone or shudder at light throttle
c: Restricted oil feed tube to the deactivation solenoids (Ford 5.0 l, TSB 26-2093)
Control software needing an update (FCA 6.4 l Hemi)

P3427.d: P3427 is set when the cylinder 4 deactivation solenoid circuit has a path to ground. GM uses it on several 2019 V8s: the DFM engine L84, the AFM engine L86 and the LT4 of the Corvette.
s: Check engine lamp after two drives
V4 or reduced mode never engages
Further circuit codes on other deactivating cylinders if the harness is damaged
c: Control wire to the cylinder 4 solenoid rubbed through to ground, e.g. by a heat shield
Moisture or oil in the solenoid connector
Damaged driver in the engine control module

P3428.d: P3428 means the wire that switches cylinder 4's deactivation solenoid is tied to voltage. GM's bulletin 20-NA-038 lists cylinders 1, 4, 6 and 7 as the ones its AFM V8s switch to V4 mode, which makes cylinder 4 a standard candidate.
c: Cylinder 4 control wire shorted to a 12 V feed
Low-resistance winding in the cylinder 4 solenoid
Overloaded output stage in the engine control module

P3429.d: P3429 stands for an open circuit to an actuator that would switch nothing but cylinder 4's exhaust valves. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, although few cylinders are deactivated as often: GM's AFM V8s (bulletin 20-NA-038), the Hemi with MDS and Mazda CX-5 and Mazda6 four-cylinders with deactivation all idle cylinder 4; Mazda's alert SA-041/18 names cylinders 1 and 4 as the deactivation area where rocker
c: Open conductor or pushed-out pin to the cylinder 4 exhaust actuator

P3430.d: P3430 would cover exhaust valves on cylinder 4 that keep opening, or stay shut, against the command while the circuit itself is sound. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Lean or rich fuel trim codes
c: Restricted oil supply to the cylinder 4 switching elements
Exhaust lifter or rocker of cylinder 4 not changing state
Oil too thin, too old or too low

P3431.d: P3431 reports a cylinder 4 exhaust actuator line shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Cylinder 4 exhaust actuator lead grounded on the block or a bracket
Internal short to ground in the exhaust actuator

P3432.d: P3432 is the last code of the cylinder 4 block and denotes an exhaust actuator control line sitting at supply voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 4 in contact with battery voltage
Exhaust actuator coil with shorted windings
Output stage of the engine control module defective

P3433.d: P3433 reports an open control circuit to the deactivation valve of cylinder 5, and GM has used it across three generations. The 2007 V6 with Displacement on Demand, which shut off cylinders 1, 3 and 5, already flagged a short or open after 30 failures in 100 samples at 250 ms above 800 rpm.
s: Oil seepage at the valve cover control valve (V6)
c: Oil leaking at the cylinder 5 control valve into its connector (GM 3.6 L V6)
Broken wire or spread terminal in the solenoid circuit
Open coil in the cylinder 5 solenoid

P3434.d: With P3434 the computer has found that cylinder 5 does not switch off or back on correctly, while the control circuit tests fine. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Oil leaking past the cylinder 5 control valve seal
Switching rocker or lifter of cylinder 5 not latching
Solenoid tip broken off in the bore

P3435.d: P3435 flags a short to ground on the control line of the cylinder 5 deactivation valve. GM documents it codewise twice: in the 2019 tables for the L84 V8, with under 0.5 ohm to ground in the driver-off state, 20 of 25 samples at 250 ms and Type B, and in an engineering bulletin for 3.6 L V6 engines (LGX, LGZ) where P3435 appears along with P3433 and P3409 when oil leaks from the rocker arm control valve.
s: Oil wetness at the valve cover around the control valve (V6)
c: Oil in the cylinder 5 valve connector creating a leakage path (GM 3.6 L V6)

P3436.d: P3436 is the short-to-power code for the cylinder 5 deactivation valve. Publicly it is documented by GM for the L84 V8 (2019), where Dynamic Fuel Management uses a dedicated valve lifter oil solenoid for each of the eight cylinders.
s: Check engine lamp after two trips
c: Control wire touching a voltage supply
Shorted coil in the cylinder 5 solenoid
Engine control module output stage defect

P3437.d: P3437 is reserved for an open circuit in a separate exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 5. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Broken wire or connector to the cylinder 5 exhaust actuator

P3438.d: P3438 describes an exhaust side of cylinder 5 that is commanded to deactivate or reactivate but does not follow, with an intact circuit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Roughness or noise while cylinders are switched off
c: Exhaust lifter or rocker of cylinder 5 slow to switch

P3439.d: P3439 would report a short to ground in the control circuit of a dedicated exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 5. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no threshold is published for it.
s: Engine runs on all cylinders only
c: Control wire of the exhaust actuator grounded

P3440.d: P3440 closes the cylinder 5 block and stands for a high signal, usually a short to supply voltage, in the circuit of a separate exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Exhaust actuator control wire shorted to voltage
Engine control module output stage fault

P3441.d: Cylinder 6 belongs to both classic V8 deactivation groups, so P3441 is a code that real engines set. On GM V8s with Active Fuel Management, which park cylinders 1, 7, 6 and 4, the 2019 tables list it for the L86 truck engine and the LT4 Corvette: with the low-side driver off, more than 200 kohm between output and ground counts as an open, and 20 failures in 25 samples (every 250 ms, from 400 rpm) store a Type B code.
s: Engine no longer drops to four-cylinder mode
Possibly circuit codes for cylinders 1, 4 and 7 as well if the shared harness is damaged
c: Solenoid harness broken or chafed through (on the 5.7 L Hemi by the manifold heat shield)
Open coil in the cylinder 6 deactivation solenoid
Loose or corroded connector at the cylinder 6 solenoid
Control module software that needs an update (Chrysler TSB 18-002-25)

P3442.d: P3442 reports that cylinder 6 does not switch off or back on as commanded although its control circuit tests fine. FCA uses it as Cylinder 6 Deactivation Control Performance on the 6.4 l Heavy Duty Hemi with MDS in RAM 2500 to 5500 trucks: bulletins 18-082-16 and 18-036-20 list it with P3402, P3426 and P3450 under a lit MIL and fix it with new PCM software.
s: Jerk or vibration when the engine changes between eight and four cylinders
Fuel consumption rises because deactivation is locked out
c: Outdated PCM calibration (FCA 6.4 l, bulletins 18-082-16 and 18-036-20)
Restricted oil feed tube to the left-bank solenoids (Ford 5.0 l, TSB 26-2093)
Oil level too low, wrong grade or worn oil, so pressure builds too slowly
Deactivating lifter of cylinder 6 not locking or unlocking

P3443.d: Here the engine computer has found the cylinder 6 solenoid's switched lead pulled to ground. GM spells out the test for its 2019 V8s (L84, L86 and the LT4 Corvette): while the low-side driver is off, an impedance under 0.5 ohm toward ground is a fault, and 20 hits among 25 checks while the powertrain relay supplies at least 11 V store a Type B code.
s: Check engine lamp on from the second faulty trip
P3441 stored at the same time on some GM controllers
c: Insulation of the cylinder 6 control wire worn through to ground
Cylinder 6 solenoid shorted internally to its housing
Moisture or oil bridging the pins of the solenoid connector
Output stage in the engine control module damaged

P3444.d: P3444 is set when the output that switches the cylinder 6 deactivation solenoid to ground still sees supply voltage while it is turned on, meaning the line has a short to power instead of a path through the coil. GM tests this on the 2019 L84, L86 and LT4 V8s with a limit of 0.5 ohm to controller power, 20 errors out of 25 samples at 250 ms intervals and Type B lamp logic.
s: Engine runs on all eight cylinders permanently
Slightly higher fuel consumption at light load
c: Cylinder 6 control wire in contact with a supply wire in the harness
Shorted turns in the cylinder 6 solenoid coil
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

P3445.d: P3445 is defined for a break in the wiring of a stand-alone actuator that would control the exhaust valves of cylinder 6. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Broken wire or loose connector at the cylinder 6 exhaust actuator
Output stage in the control module faulty

P3446.d: P3446 stands for an exhaust valve on cylinder 6 that does not follow a deactivation or reactivation command although its circuit is intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Knock-like noise or vibration when the cylinder is switched back on
c: Exhaust lifter of cylinder 6 switching late or not at all
Oil pressure too low for reliable switching

P3447.d: P3447 is about a ground fault on the lead of a stand-alone exhaust actuator for cylinder 6. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 6 chafed against the engine
Internal short to ground in the exhaust actuator
Damaged driver in the engine control module

P3448.d: If cylinder 6 had its own exhaust valve actuator, P3448 would report its control line shorted to battery voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Exhaust actuator wire touching a supply line
Shorted turns in the exhaust actuator coil of cylinder 6
Engine control module output stage faulty

P3449.d: P3449 tells you the engine computer lost continuity in the circuit to the cylinder 7 deactivation solenoid. Chrysler documents it twice for the 5.7 L Hemi with MDS: a 2025 bulletin for the 2023 RAM 1500 eTorque lists it next to a cylinder 7 misfire (P0307) and fixes it with new PCM software, and a STAR case names P3449 first when the driver-side manifold heat shield has worn through the MDS harness at the rear of the
s: Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 7 (P0307) on the 5.7 L Hemi
c: MDS harness at the rear of the driver-side head worn through by the manifold heat shield (5.7 L Hemi)
PCM calibration needing an update (Chrysler TSB 18-002-25)

P3450.d: P3450 reports that cylinder 7 does not deactivate or reactivate as commanded while its solenoid circuit checks out. FCA lists it as Cylinder 7 Deactivation Control Performance for the 6.4 l Heavy Duty Hemi with MDS (RAM 2500 to 5500, bulletins 18-082-16 and 18-036-20): the MIL lights and a PCM reflash cures it, with an optional calibration that also eases drone and shudder in MDS mode.
s: Ticking noise from the valve train
c: Restricted oil feed tube to the left-bank solenoids (Ford 5.0 l, TSB 26-2093)
Outdated PCM calibration (FCA 6.4 l, bulletins 18-082-16 and 18-036-20)
Locking pins in a cylinder 7 lifter sticking from wear or dirt
Insufficient or aged oil delaying the switch

P3451.d: P3451 means the switched ground line of the cylinder 7 deactivation solenoid has contact with ground somewhere along its way. GM documents the check for the L84 and L86 trucks and the LT4 Corvette (2019): with the driver off, less than 0.5 ohm to ground, 20 hits in 25 samples taken every 250 ms, Type B, meaning the warning lamp waits for a second faulty trip.
s: Check engine lamp on after two trips
P3449 may be stored as well
No four-cylinder mode, higher fuel use
c: Cylinder 7 control wire pinched or chafed to ground
Oil or water inside the solenoid connector
Defective driver in the engine control module

P3452.d: Unlike the open and ground-short checks, GM can only detect P3452 while the cylinder 7 solenoid driver is switched on, because a short to supply voltage shows up as an output that will not pull low when it should. The 2019 tables for the L84, L86 and LT4 set the limit at 0.5 ohm to controller power and need 20 errors out of 25 samples, Type B.
s: Check engine lamp on, often only after longer warm drives
c: Cylinder 7 control wire shorted to a voltage feed
Low-resistance coil in the cylinder 7 solenoid

P3453.d: P3453 is the code SAE assigns to an open circuit in a dedicated exhaust valve actuator for cylinder 7. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Interrupted wire to the cylinder 7 exhaust actuator

P3454.d: P3454 covers an exhaust valve on cylinder 7 that does not switch as commanded, with no electrical fault on its control circuit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Hard knock or jolt when cylinder 7 is reactivated
c: Exhaust lifter of cylinder 7 stuck in the unlocked state
Oil pressure or oil quality inadequate for switching
Exhaust control valve slow or sticking

P3455.d: P3455 points to a ground fault on the line that would drive an exhaust-only actuator on cylinder 7. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Rough running or misfire on cylinder 7 if the actuator pulls in unbidden
c: Actuator wire chafed through against the cylinder head or a heat shield
Actuator coil shorted to its housing
Output stage in the engine control module damaged

P3456.d: P3456 would flag a cylinder 7 exhaust valve actuator whose control line is shorted to supply voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Engine does not enter reduced-cylinder mode
c: Actuator wire of cylinder 7 shorted to battery voltage
Exhaust actuator coil with shorted turns
Current driver in the control module failed

P3457.d: Cylinder 8 is not among the cylinders that classic Active Fuel Management or Chrysler's MDS shut off (both use 1, 4, 6 and 7), so P3457 is documented only for newer designs. GM's 2019 tables list it for the L84 with Dynamic Fuel Management, which can deactivate every cylinder: more than 200 kohm with the low-side driver off, 20 of 25 samples every 250 ms from 425 rpm, Type B.
s: P3459 may be stored alongside on some GM controllers
c: Wire to the cylinder 8 solenoid broken or chafed in the lifter valley harness
Open winding in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Poor contact at the solenoid connector
Engine control module output stage faulty

P3458.d: P3458 describes a cylinder 8 that does not deactivate or reactivate as commanded although its control circuit is electrically fine. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine lamp on, sometimes going out again
Shake or roughness in light-load cruising
c: Cylinder 8 deactivation lifter not unlocking or relocking
Oil pressure too low or oil aerated
Cylinder 8 solenoid valve sluggish or its screen blocked
False entry after low voltage while cranking, fixed by ECM update (GM analogue 20-NA-204)

P3459.d: When the ground-side control line of the cylinder 8 deactivation solenoid touches ground, the ECM stores P3459. GM publishes this test for the 2019 L84 V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management: driver off, impedance below 0.5 ohm to ground, a minimum of 11 V on the relay feed and 425 rpm, 20 errors in 25 samples, Type B.
s: Check engine lamp on after the second trip
Engine runs on all eight cylinders at all times
c: Cylinder 8 control wire grounded through damaged insulation
Internal short in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Output driver in the engine control module damaged

P3460.d: P3460 reports a short to supply voltage on the control circuit of the cylinder 8 deactivation solenoid, found while the output is switched on. GM lists it for the 2019 L84: under 0.5 ohm between output and controller power, 20 of 25 samples spaced 250 ms apart, Type B, with the same 11 V and 425 rpm enable limits as the other cylinder 8 circuit checks.
s: Cylinder deactivation inactive, slightly higher fuel use
c: Cylinder 8 control wire in contact with a voltage source
Shorted turns in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Faulty driver in the engine control module

P3461.d: In the J2012 scheme, P3461 marks lost continuity to an exhaust-side actuator of its own on cylinder 8. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Wire or plug to the cylinder 8 exhaust actuator broken

P3462.d: With P3462 the ECM would be saying that the exhaust valve of cylinder 8 ignores deactivation commands even though nothing is wrong electrically. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Exhaust lifter of cylinder 8 failing to relock in time
Oil supply to the lifter gallery insufficient

P3463.d: P3463 would mean that the control line of a dedicated cylinder 8 exhaust actuator is shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Engine stays on all eight cylinders
c: Cylinder 8 exhaust actuator wire shorted to the engine block
Exhaust actuator shorted to ground internally
Driver stage in the engine control module faulty

P3464.d: P3464 is stored once the line to a stand-alone cylinder 8 exhaust actuator sits at a high level, typically a wire touching battery voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Engine keeps running on all eight cylinders, slightly higher fuel use
c: Control wire of the cylinder 8 actuator touching a battery feed
Shorted turns in the actuator coil, resistance far too low
Output stage in the engine control module failed

P3465.d: P3465 flags an open circuit to the actuator meant to shut down cylinder 9 or hold its intake valve closed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Slightly higher fuel consumption at part load
c: Broken or chafed wire to the cylinder 9 actuator
Open coil in the cylinder 9 solenoid
Loose or corroded connector at the solenoid pack
Output stage in the engine control module failed

P3466.d: P3466 is the plausibility test for cylinder 9: its actuator circuit is electrically sound, yet the cylinder fails to change state when the engine computer commands it. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Rough running while switching between full and partial mode
c: Oil level, pressure or quality too poor to switch cylinder 9
Leak at the oil tubes or solenoid pack feeding cylinder 9
Solenoid valve slow or sticking mechanically

P3467.d: With P3467 the control line of the cylinder 9 deactivation or intake valve actuator reads too low, which usually means it is touching ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Possible misfire on cylinder 9 if the actuator stays energised
c: Cylinder 9 control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the cylinder 9 solenoid
Faulty driver in the engine control module

P3468.d: P3468 indicates that the control circuit for the cylinder 9 deactivation or intake valve actuator is pulled high, typically by a short to battery voltage that the module notices once it switches the output on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Engine runs on all cylinders at all times
c: Cylinder 9 control wire touching a supply wire
Shorted turns in the cylinder 9 solenoid coil
Output stage of the engine control module damaged

P3469.d: P3469 is set when the circuit driving a separate exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 9 is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Open or chafed wire to the cylinder 9 exhaust actuator
Exhaust actuator coil of cylinder 9 open
Connector at the exhaust actuator loose or corroded

P3470.d: P3470 covers a cylinder 9 exhaust valve that does not follow its deactivation command although the control circuit shows no electrical fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Knock or jolt when cylinder 9 comes back in
c: Exhaust switching element of cylinder 9 stuck
Insufficient oil pressure for the exhaust switch

P3471.d: A low reading on the control line of the cylinder 9 exhaust valve actuator triggers P3471, most often a wire grounded against the engine or body. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 9 grounded
Internal short in the exhaust actuator

P3472.d: P3472 records a high voltage level on the cylinder 9 exhaust valve control circuit, the pattern of a wire shorted to a supply feed or of a coil with shorted windings. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Cylinder deactivation switched off by the control module
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 9 shorted to voltage
Shorted windings in the exhaust actuator

P3473.d: P3473 reports an open circuit to the deactivation or intake valve actuator of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Engine no longer switches to reduced-cylinder mode
c: Wire to the cylinder 10 actuator open or chafed
Corroded or loose connector at cylinder 10

P3474.d: P3474 is about function rather than wiring: cylinder 10 should shut down or come back, but measured engine behaviour says it did not, while its control circuit is intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Tapping noise from the valve train
c: Oil pressure or oil condition not sufficient to switch cylinder 10
Lifter or cam sleeve at cylinder 10 sticking
Oil screen or passage to the cylinder 10 actuator blocked

P3475.d: P3475 points to a short to ground on the circuit that controls deactivation or the intake valve of cylinder 10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Cylinder 10 control wire grounded through chafing

P3476.d: P3476 is logged when the control circuit of the cylinder 10 deactivation or intake valve actuator sits at too high a level, usually a short to a battery-fed wire found while the output is active. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Cylinder deactivation locked out for the drive
c: Cylinder 10 control wire shorted to a supply
Cylinder 10 actuator coil with shorted turns

P3477.d: P3477 belongs to engines that switch the exhaust valve of cylinder 10 through its own actuator, and it reports that this actuator's circuit is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Wire to the cylinder 10 exhaust actuator interrupted
Exhaust actuator coil of cylinder 10 open

P3478.d: P3478 describes a cylinder 10 exhaust valve that does not switch as commanded although its actuator circuit is fine. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Harsh jolt as cylinder 10 is reactivated
c: Exhaust switching element at cylinder 10 stuck
Oil pressure too low for the exhaust switch

P3479.d: P3479 shows a short to ground, or another cause of a low signal, on the control line of the cylinder 10 exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 10 shorted to ground

P3480.d: If the control line of the cylinder 10 exhaust valve actuator is held near supply voltage, the engine computer stores P3480. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 10 shorted to a feed
Shorted windings in the exhaust actuator coil

P3481.d: P3481 marks an open circuit to the actuator for deactivation or the intake valve of cylinder 11, a cylinder only V12 and W12 engines possess. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Engine stays on all twelve cylinders
c: Wire to the cylinder 11 actuator broken
Actuator connector at cylinder 11 loose or corroded
Driver stage in the engine control module failed

P3482.d: P3482 is the functional check for cylinder 11: the actuator circuit is electrically fine, but the cylinder does not actually go dormant or wake up when told to. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Contaminated or insufficient oil for switching cylinder 11
Worn or sticking locking pins at cylinder 11
Oil screen to the cylinder 11 actuator clogged

P3483.d: P3483 is stored for a low signal on the control circuit of the cylinder 11 deactivation or intake valve actuator, in practice a short to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Cylinder 11 control line shorted to ground

P3484.d: P3484 signals that the control circuit of the cylinder 11 deactivation or intake valve actuator is too high, for example because its wire is shorted to a battery feed and the module detects it when switching the output on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Cylinder 11 control wire touching battery voltage
Cylinder 11 actuator coil with shorted turns

P3485.d: P3485 is triggered by an open circuit on a separate exhaust valve actuator at cylinder 11. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Engine no longer drops to half its cylinders
c: Open wire to the cylinder 11 exhaust actuator
Coil of the cylinder 11 exhaust actuator open
Connector at the exhaust actuator corroded

P3486.d: P3486 flags a functional problem with the exhaust valve of cylinder 11: the circuit is healthy, but the valve does not reach the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Exhaust switching element of cylinder 11 jammed
Oil supply inadequate for exhaust switching

P3487.d: P3487 would tell of a grounded control wire feeding a dedicated exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 11. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; cylinders 9 to 12 only exist on engines with nine or more, and J2012 keeps these codes for them.
c: Actuator wire chafed through to engine ground
Actuator coil shorted to its housing
Moisture in the actuator connector bridging to ground

P3488.d: With P3488, the cylinder 11 exhaust actuator line sits too high, most often since the wire has picked up battery voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; cylinders 9 to 12 only exist on engines with nine or more, and J2012 keeps these codes for them.
s: Engine stays on all twelve cylinders
c: Control wire of the cylinder 11 actuator touching a battery feed
Shorted turns in the actuator coil
Output stage in the engine control module failed

P3489.d: P3489 reports that the circuit to the actuator for deactivation or the intake valve of cylinder 12, the highest cylinder number in this code series, is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Engine no longer runs in reduced-cylinder mode
Somewhat higher fuel use on the highway
c: Wire to the cylinder 12 actuator open or chafed
Loose or corroded connector at cylinder 12
Output stage of the control module failed

P3490.d: P3490 concerns the mechanical result on cylinder 12: the actuator circuit passes its electrical checks, but the cylinder does not deactivate or reactivate as intended. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Oil pressure or quality inadequate to switch cylinder 12
Leak in the oil supply to the cylinder 12 actuator

P3491.d: A ground fault on the control line of the cylinder 12 deactivation or intake valve actuator produces P3491. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Cylinder 12 control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the cylinder 12 actuator

P3492.d: P3492 records a high condition on the control circuit of the cylinder 12 deactivation or intake valve actuator, generally a short to a supply voltage seen while the output is commanded on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Engine runs permanently on twelve cylinders
c: Cylinder 12 control wire shorted to supply voltage
Shorted turns in the cylinder 12 actuator

P3493.d: P3493 applies to a separately controlled exhaust valve on cylinder 12 and reports that its actuator circuit is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Wire to the cylinder 12 exhaust actuator open
Coil of the cylinder 12 exhaust actuator interrupted

P3494.d: P3494 is set when the exhaust valve of cylinder 12 does not follow its command although the actuator circuit is electrically intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
s: Jolt or knock on reactivation of cylinder 12
c: Exhaust switching element at cylinder 12 sticking
Oil pressure or quality insufficient for the exhaust switch

P3495.d: P3495 points to a low signal, usually a short to ground, on the control line of the cylinder 12 exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 12 grounded

P3496.d: P3496 is the final code of the per-cylinder valve block: it marks the cylinder 12 exhaust valve control circuit as too high, typically a short to battery voltage or a coil with shorted turns. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders.
c: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 12 shorted to battery voltage
Shorted turns in the exhaust actuator coil

P3497.d: P3497 is the bank 2 counterpart of P3400: the control unit concludes that deactivation on the bank that lacks cylinder 1 is failing as a whole, and it blames no single cylinder circuit. Honda's VCM V6 links it to rocker arm oil pressure switch C (P3400 belongs to switch B); bulletin 13-055 for the 2013 Odyssey and Pilot shows both codes after cold starts with oil pressure above 92 psi, which moved the spool valves an
s: Misfire codes on bank 2 cylinders, mostly after a cold start
Rough idle while the engine warms up
Reduced-cylinder mode no longer used, higher fuel use
c: Excess oil pressure on cold start, e.g. weak relief valve spring
Low oil level, wrong grade or overdue oil change on bank 2
Switchable rocker arm or lifter on bank 2 sticking or not latching
Rocker arm oil pressure switch of bank 2 reporting wrongly
Engine control software needing an update

P3498.d: P3498 flags a mechanical failure on cylinder 1: the control unit commanded it off, but its valves kept opening. This differs from P3402, which concerns the control side, and from the wiring codes P3401, P3403 and P3404.
s: Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 1 (P0301)
Clatter from the cylinder head and loss of power
Cylinder deactivation no longer used, higher fuel use
c: Switchable rocker arm of cylinder 1 dropped out or broken (Mazda)
Deactivation lifter of cylinder 1 stays locked (GM DFM)
Lifter oil solenoid of cylinder 1 sticking or with protruding pole piece
Overdue oil changes or wrong oil grade

P3499.d: P3499 reports that cylinder 2 did not stop exchanging gas when told to deactivate. On GM's DFM V8s (L84, L87) one oil solenoid in the lifter valley feeds both lifters of the cylinder; oil pressure pushes spring-loaded pins inward which lets the outer lifter shell ride the cam while the valve remains closed.
s: Higher fuel consumption because cylinder 2 is no longer skipped
c: Locking pins in the cylinder 2 lifters do not retract
Lifter oil solenoid of cylinder 2 not delivering oil pressure
Code stored without a real fault, ECM software update needed

P349A.d: P349A states that cylinder 3 kept its valves working while the engine computer had switched it off. GM picks this up on its L84 and L87 V8s through manifold pressure that stays too high during the skipped strokes, Type B after 22 failed checks out of 25.
s: Code stored in history with no noticeable concern
Check engine lamp on if the fault is real
Ticking noise or higher fuel use
c: Voltage dip at cranking disabled the outputs, ECM software outdated
Deactivation lifter of cylinder 3 does not unlock
Lifter oil solenoid of cylinder 3 sticking
Low or aged oil slowing the switching

P349B.d: P349B is set when cylinder 4 fails to shut its valves on command. On Mazda's 2.5 l Skyactiv-G with cylinder deactivation (CX-5 and Mazda6, 2018-2019), cylinders 1 and 4 can be switched off; service alerts SA-041/18 and SA-022/19 tie P349B, P3498, P3400, P0304 and P0340 to a rocker arm that fell out of place or broke.
s: Rough idle and misfire on cylinder 4 (P0304)
Clatter or knocking from the valve cover area
c: Rocker arm of cylinder 4 fallen out of place or broken (Mazda)
Long oil change intervals or unsuitable oil
Deactivation lifter of cylinder 4 stuck locked (GM DFM)
Oil control solenoid of cylinder 4 faulty

P349C.d: P349C means that cylinder 5 stayed active although the engine computer had requested a skip. GM documents it for its Dynamic Fuel Management V8s (L84 with 5.3 l, L87 with 6.2 l), where every cylinder may be skipped; the classic AFM V8s rest only cylinders 1, 7, 6 and 4.
s: Engine no longer skips cylinders, fuel use rises
c: Lifter oil solenoid of cylinder 5 faulty, pole piece protruding
Lifters of cylinder 5 do not unlock
Dirt in the oil blocking the solenoid or lifter bores

P349D.d: P349D indicates that cylinder 6 drew in and pushed out air during events in which it should have stayed sealed. The test logic rests on a simple effect: every intake stroke leaves a dip in manifold pressure, so a resting cylinder should leave none.
s: Higher fuel use in light-load cruising
c: Locking pins of the cylinder 6 lifters do not release
Low oil level or degraded oil
Intake leak or MAP sensor fault distorting the pressure pulses

P349E.d: P349E covers cylinder 7: deactivation was commanded, yet the cylinder kept its valve events. In GM's DFM design the intake lifter is unlocked first, while the exhaust lifter can only release once its cam lobe is back on the base circle; a sluggish pin therefore tends to leave the exhaust side working.
c: Sluggish locking pin, mostly in the exhaust lifter of cylinder 7
Oil solenoid of cylinder 7 not opening fully

P349F.d: P349F reports that cylinder 8 failed to go quiet when commanded. California's OBD rule requires makers to analyse every plausible hydraulic or mechanical failure of variable valve systems and mentions, among its examples, a lift-mechanism pin of one cylinder that will not shift; codes like this one follow from that duty.
s: Check engine lamp on after two trips
Engine stays on all cylinders, fuel use rises
c: Lifter of cylinder 8 stuck in its locked state
Weak or sticking oil solenoid of cylinder 8
Sludge or debris in the lifter oil passages
Stored after a voltage dip at cranking, ECM software update needed

P34A0.d: P34A0 is reserved for a cylinder 9 that keeps its valves moving after the engine computer has ordered it off, which presumes an engine with at least nine cylinders and per-cylinder valve switching. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Switching lifter or rocker of cylinder 9 stuck
Oil control valve for the deactivation not switching

P34A1.d: P34A1 would mean that cylinder 10 kept opening its valves while it was supposed to be deactivated. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; it only makes sense on V10, V12 or W12 engines.
c: Switching element of cylinder 10 not unlocking
Oil level too low or oil aged

P34A2.d: P34A2 names a mechanical deactivation fault on cylinder 11: the valves continued to operate although the cylinder had been switched off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Rough running when one bank is shut down
c: Valve switching element of cylinder 11 jammed
Oil pressure supply to the switching parts disturbed

P34A3.d: P34A3 closes the series at the twelfth cylinder: cylinder 12 was commanded to deactivate, but its valves did not stop. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Lifter or rocker switching element of cylinder 12 stuck
Oil control valve of the deactivation sticking

P34A4.d: P34A4 flags an electrical problem of any kind in the temperature sensor circuit of intake camshaft actuator A on bank 1: a wire broken somewhere, a plug that has worked loose, or a value no valid window accepts. Such a sensor belongs to electrically driven phasers; an Aisin patent places it on the motor driver board and reduces motor current once that board stays hot.
s: Intake cam phasing on bank 1 restricted or held in its base position
Often no noticeable change while driving
c: Plug at the actuator loose or corroded, sensor wire broken
Temperature sensor in the actuator or its electronics failed
Fault in the module that drives the electric phaser

P34A5.d: P34A5 means the temperature reported for intake cam actuator A on bank 1 passes the electrical checks yet makes no sense. Nissan describes the code for the 2018 Pathfinder (R52) and the Infiniti QX60 built before 18 December 2017: the MIL came on after starts at ambient temperatures around or below 0 °C.
s: Check engine light on, often after a cold start
c: Software of the electric valve timing module (Nissan 2018: cold-start false alarm)
Temperature sensor drifting out of its expected range
Intermittent contact at the actuator plug

P34A6.d: With P34A6 the temperature signal from the intake cam actuator on bank 1 sits under its minimum. No source available to us names the sensor type.
s: Intake phasing on bank 1 limited, less pulling power
c: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed at the cylinder head)
Actuator really overheated by a sluggish phaser

P34A7.d: P34A7 is set when the temperature sensor of intake camshaft actuator A on bank 1 delivers a voltage above its upper limit. Most often the sensor wire or its ground is interrupted, or the signal touches a supply voltage; with an NTC-type sensor this reads as an implausibly cold actuator.
s: Mostly no noticeable effect while driving
c: Signal or ground wire of the sensor interrupted
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage

P34A8.d: P34A8 mirrors P34A4 on bank 2: the module detects an open or otherwise faulty circuit at the temperature sensor of intake cam actuator A on the side without cylinder 1. Only V and boxer engines have this bank.
c: Plug at the bank 2 actuator corroded or not latched
Harness chafed near the cylinder head

P34A9.d: P34A9 covers the plausibility check of the temperature sensor at intake cam actuator A on bank 2. Nissan names it together with P34A5 in bulletins NTB18-016 (2018 Pathfinder) and ITB18-009 (2018 QX60): vehicles built before 18 December 2017 could store one or both codes and switch on the MIL when started in freezing weather.
s: Check engine light on after a start in freezing weather
Engine runs normally in most cases
c: Poor contact at the bank 2 actuator plug

P34AA.d: P34AA reports that the temperature sensor of the bank 2 intake cam actuator signals a voltage below its permitted range. Whether that equals a hot reading depends on the sensor design, which no public source names; with the common NTC thermistor it would mimic overheating, and the controller could limit the actuator current or stop phasing on that bank.
s: Intake phasing on bank 2 suspended, slightly less power
c: Signal wire grounded against the cylinder head
Cables pinched during earlier engine work

P34AB.d: P34AB stands for a voltage above the upper limit at the temperature sensor of intake cam actuator A, bank 2. An interrupted signal or ground line is the classic cause, as is a short to a higher voltage; a plug pushed off during a service visit often explains it.
s: Intake phasing on bank 2 held back
c: Plug at the actuator off or not latched after service
Signal shorted to a higher voltage

P34AC.d: P34AC covers any electrical fault in the circuit of position sensor A of the intake cam actuator on bank 1. On engines with an electric intake phaser this sensor tells the controller where the drive motor stands.
s: Intake cam held in its base position, less torque at low revs
Rougher cold start, slightly higher consumption
c: Actuator harness open or shorted, plug loose
Position sensor in the electric actuator failed (actuator replacement)
Electric valve timing control module faulty

P34AD.d: P34AD covers a plausibility fault: the position sensor A signal from the intake actuator on bank 1 is electrically present but does not agree with what else the module knows. On the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander, which turns its intake phaser electrically, the control module checks the motor position against the phase seen by the intake camshaft sensor and logs P34AD when the two disagree; wiring faults and the actuator
s: Intake cam timing fixed, weaker response at low revs
Possibly accompanying timing codes such as P0011
c: Electric actuator worn, sticking or slipping
Actuator position not relearned after repair
Intake camshaft sensor signal or timing drive disturbed

P34AE.d: P34AE says the voltage from position sensor A on the bank 1 intake side remains under its minimum. The 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander, whose intake cam is moved by an electric motor, evaluates the code in the electric valve timing module and points to an open or shorted actuator circuit or a faulty actuator; unlike the circuit and high codes, no delay time is stated.
s: Less pulling power at low revs
Rougher running after a cold start
c: Hall sensor in the actuator motor shorted (actuator replacement)

P34AF.d: P34AF is logged when position sensor A on the bank 1 intake phaser reports a voltage above its upper limit for at least one second. Mitsubishi covers the code in its 2022 Outlander manual and, besides the harness, points to the Hall sensor of motor 1 in the electric actuator – a hint that position sensor A is a Hall element inside the phaser motor.
s: Intake phaser held in its base position, reduced power
c: Sensor ground open or plug corroded
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Hall sensor of the actuator motor failed (actuator replacement)

P34B0.d: P34B0 concerns the electrical circuit of position sensor A of the intake cam actuator on bank 2, so it only concerns V and boxer engines. No manufacturer publishes it.
s: Bank 2 intake phasing held in its base position
Possibly less power and uneven running between banks
c: Plug or harness to the bank 2 actuator open or shorted
Position sensor in the actuator failed

P34B1.d: P34B1 means the intake-side position sensor A of bank 2 delivers an electrically sound but implausible value. No public manufacturer document uses this code.
s: Bank 2 intake timing fixed, reduced power
Possibly further timing codes such as P0021
c: Actuator on bank 2 sticking or worn
Learned actuator position lost or software outdated

P34B2.d: P34B2 is set when position sensor A on the intake phaser of bank 2 delivers a voltage below its permitted window. Public manufacturer information on this code is lacking.
s: Possibly codes from other sensors on the same supply

P34B3.d: P34B3 marks a signal above the upper limit from position sensor A on the intake phaser of bank 2. An interrupted ground, a signal wire touching a supply voltage or a worn-out sensor are the usual findings.
s: Bank 2 intake phaser held at its base angle
c: Signal wire touching a supply voltage
Hall sensor in the actuator defective (actuator replacement)

P34B4.d: P34B4 reports that the circuit of the temperature sensor on camshaft actuator B, bank 1, cannot be evaluated: an open line, a disconnected plug or a reading that fits no valid state. In the supplier list of NTN-SNR the letter B stands for the outlet camshaft, so the code targets an exhaust phaser turned by an electric motor whose electronics need heat protection.
s: Exhaust cam timing on bank 1 fixed or limited
c: Plug at the exhaust actuator not seated or wire broken
Temperature sensor in the actuator electronics failed
Faulty input stage in the controlling module

P34B5.d: P34B5 is the rationality check for the temperature reading of exhaust-side actuator B on bank 1: the circuit is intact, yet the value or its behaviour is not believable. CARB asks for such checks on VVT input sensors wherever feasible, ideally catching readings that are wrongly high as well as wrongly low.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, sometimes only after a cold start
No noticeable change in engine behaviour in most cases
c: Module software judging the value wrongly (update available?)
Temperature sensor in the actuator drifting

P34B6.d: Circuit Low means the voltage on the signal wire of the exhaust actuator B temperature sensor (bank 1) stays under its lower limit. Which temperature that stands for depends on a sensor curve that no public source gives; with a thermistor whose resistance falls as it warms, a short to ground would look like extreme heat.
s: Exhaust phasing on bank 1 reduced, slightly rougher idle possible
c: Signal wire chafed through and touching ground
Sensor element shorted inside the actuator
Actuator driver genuinely overheated by a binding phaser

P34B7.d: P34B7 sets when the heat reading delivered by exhaust actuator B, bank 1, sits above its upper limit. Electrically this points to an open signal line, a detached sensor ground or contact with battery or reference voltage; with a negative-coefficient element the module would see an implausibly cold actuator.
s: Exhaust cam on bank 1 held in its default position
c: Signal line or sensor ground interrupted, plug corroded
Signal line shorted to a supply wire
Sensor element open inside the actuator

P34B8.d: P34B8 is the circuit fault for the heat sensor inside exhaust camshaft actuator B of bank 2, the row without cylinder 1 on a V or flat engine. If P34B4 is stored at the same time, a shared feed, a common ground or the control module is more likely than two failed sensors at once.
s: Exhaust phasing on bank 2 restricted, banks may run slightly unevenly
c: Connector or harness at the bank 2 exhaust actuator open
Shared supply or ground faulty (when bank 1 also reports)
Temperature sensor in the bank 2 actuator failed

P34B9.d: With P34B9 the bank 2 exhaust actuator reports a temperature that is electrically valid but does not make sense. A two-bank engine offers an obvious yardstick: after a long cold soak both exhaust actuators should read almost the same, and under equal load they should warm alike.
c: Contact resistance at the plug shifting the value

P34BA.d: P34BA tells that the temperature signal from bank 2's exhaust actuator is pulled under its lower limit. Typical sources are a signal wire that has found ground, for instance where the harness runs close to hot exhaust parts, or a sensor element shorted inside the actuator.
s: Bank 2 exhaust timing limited, possibly with additional timing codes
c: Harness near exhaust parts damaged, signal shorted to ground
Sensor element shorted inside the bank 2 actuator
Input of the controlling module faulty

P34BB.d: P34BB is stored when the bank 2 exhaust actuator's temperature signal stays above its window – typically a broken signal line, a loosened ground connection or contact with a supply wire. Because the module can no longer see how warm the actuator driver is, it lacks what it needs to protect it; Aisin's design, for comparison, ends its current reduction only after the reading has stayed below a return threshold for som
s: Bank 2 exhaust cam held in a safe position
c: Signal line broken or sensor ground loose
Signal line touching a supply wire
Sensor open inside the bank 2 actuator

P34BC.d: P34BC means the module cannot make sense of the wiring of sensor A, which reports where actuator B on bank 1 stands. Read against the NTN-SNR list, actuator B is the exhaust-side one.
s: Exhaust-side adjustment on bank 1 switched off
c: Connector at the exhaust actuator unplugged or corroded, wire broken
Sensor integrated in the actuator failed (actuator replacement)

P34BD.d: P34BD has a documented user. Mercedes-Benz lists P34BD09 in bulletin LI05.20-P-080192, dated 14 January 2026, for M176/M177 V8 engines with CAMTRONIC, used for example in the AMG C 63 and E 63, the G 550 and the Maybach GLS 600.
s: CAMTRONIC in limp-home mode, often with further CAMTRONIC codes
c: Engine control software outdated (Mercedes M176/M177: update)
CAMTRONIC actuator of a superseded part number

P34BE.d: For P34BE, too, a Mercedes-Benz text exists: the CAMTRONIC bulletin covering the M176 and M177 eight-cylinders reads P34BE00 as the signal of exhaust solenoid 1, bank 1, being grounded. That fits the generic meaning, a signal under its lower limit.
s: CAMTRONIC limp-home, exhaust valve lift on bank 1 no longer switched
c: Heat-damaged harness above the bulkhead, signal shorted to ground
Sensor inside the CAMTRONIC actuator shorted (older part number)
Engine control software not up to date

P34BF.d: P34BF: on bank 1, sensor A of the camshaft B actuator, i.e. the exhaust side, sends more voltage than allowed.
s: Exhaust adjustment on bank 1 kept in its reference position
c: Sensor ground interrupted or plug corroded
Signal line shorted to a supply wire
Sensor in the exhaust actuator open internally

P34C0.d: P34C0 is the generic circuit fault of position sensor A belonging to camshaft actuator B of bank 2 and therefore appears only on V-type or other two-bank engines. Mercedes-Benz files the bank 2 exhaust feedback of its CAMTRONIC V8 (M176/M177) under neighbouring codes – P34C1 for an implausible signal, P34C2 for a grounded one – but P34C0 itself is absent from its bulletin, and no other carmaker has published it.
c: Wiring or plug at the bank 2 exhaust actuator open
Shared sensor feed or ground faulty (if P34BC is also stored)
Sensor in the bank 2 actuator failed

P34C1.d: Mercedes-Benz names P34C109 for the exhaust side of bank 2 on its CAMTRONIC V8s: the signal from the sensor at solenoid 1 is wrong although the circuit is intact, entered as a component fault. CARB explains why such a check exists, since even a single cylinder pin on a lift mechanism not moving into place is a failure mode that VVT monitoring has to cover.
s: CAMTRONIC limp-home, often together with P005C
c: CAMTRONIC actuator of an older part number (Mercedes: replace)
Engine control software needs an update
Actuator pin sticking or moving too slowly

P34C2.d: Mercedes-Benz documents this code as P34C200: on cylinder bank 2, the feedback line of CAMTRONIC exhaust solenoid 1 is grounded. The code is one of sixteen that bulletin LI05.20-P-080192 groups together for engine types M176 and M177, found in AMG 63 models as well as S-Class, G-Class and GLS cars.
s: CAMTRONIC limp-home, exhaust lift on bank 2 fixed
c: Harness near the windshield heat-damaged, signal to ground
Sensor in the bank 2 CAMTRONIC actuator shorted

P34C3.d: P34C3 completes the sensor group of actuator B: on bank 2, sensor A watching the exhaust-side actuator puts out a voltage beyond its permitted range. A broken sensor ground, an open signal path or contact with a feed line are the usual causes.
s: Bank 2 exhaust adjustment held in base position
c: Signal line in contact with a supply wire
Sensor in the bank 2 exhaust actuator faulty

P34C4.d: P34C4 is logged when the output stage feeding the bank 1 intake actuator A reports that its current or its own temperature has passed the permitted limit. The code belongs to electric phasers, where a small motor instead of an oil valve turns the camshaft.
s: Intake timing on bank 1 no longer adjusted, held at a fixed angle
Weaker pull at low revs, rougher idle on a cold engine
c: Phaser stiff or held against its stop, motor draws high current for long
Low or sludged engine oil making the phaser hard to turn
Winding or motor lead of the bank 1 actuator shorted
Output stage or its sensors in the phaser control module faulty

P34C5.d: P34C5 mirrors P34C4 on bank 2 for intake actuator A: the driver powering the electric phaser motor on the second cylinder bank has measured too much current or run too hot and protects itself. Only V or boxer engines with one electric intake phaser per bank can log it.
s: Bank 2 intake timing frozen, banks run unevenly
Slightly rough idle and less torque at low engine speed
c: Bank 2 phaser stiff or stuck at an end stop
Motor lead to the bank 2 actuator chafed or shorted
Electric motor of the bank 2 actuator worn or internally shorted
Bank 2 output stage in the phaser control module faulty

P34C6.d: P34C6 concerns actuator B, which NTN-SNR assigns to the exhaust camshaft, on bank 1: the stage driving it signals overcurrent or overheating. That presumes an electrically powered exhaust phaser, and none is documented in public sources.
s: Exhaust cam timing on bank 1 fixed in its default position
Slightly higher fuel use, minor loss of smoothness
c: Exhaust phaser on bank 1 stiff, motor overloaded
Short in the motor wiring of actuator B, bank 1
Output stage for actuator B damaged or overheated

P34C7.d: P34C7 closes the group of four driver-load codes: on bank 2 the power stage of the exhaust-side actuator B reports current or temperature above its limit. NTN-SNR ties it to outlet adjustment on the second bank.
s: Bank 2 exhaust timing no longer varied
Usually only small changes in how the engine runs
c: Bank 2 exhaust phaser seized or poorly lubricated
Motor wiring of actuator B, bank 2, shorted or heat-damaged
Driver overheating from poor cooling or a module fault

P34C8.d: P34C8 does not point at one actuator or bank; it says the separate controller for cam adjustment is not working properly in itself. Mitsubishi defines it for the 2022 Outlander: with the ignition on, the controller of the electric intake phaser detects an internal CPU error, and the module is the only listed cause.
s: Cam phasing held at its reference position
Rougher cold start and fixed idle speed
Noticeably less torque, higher fuel use
c: Internal processor fault in the cam adjustment control module
Module supply or harness heat-damaged or with poor contact
